name: Lamp
description: Keep customers informed with a status page and clear incident updates.

capabilities.description: One page showing overall status, component states, unresolved incidents, upcoming maintenance, and uptime, served from a pre-rendered snapshot.
Public task guides built from repository Markdown and served on the app host beside the landing page.
The same snapshot published as an Atom feed and as a one-script-tag status banner for the buyer's own product.
Grouped, ordered services with a public state, a note, and an append-only state history.
Uptime computed from component state history over a 90-day window, with the counting rule stated on the page and corrections recomputed.
Investigating to Resolved lifecycle with an immutable public timeline, derived impact, and an overdue-update signal for operators.

A fixed template of who is affected, impact, what still works, and a next-update commitment for active incidents. Resolved updates carry no next-update promise. The shared public renderer supplies previews and publication is atomic.
Windows that start and complete themselves, set and restore component states, remind subscribers, and admit overrun on the page.
Confirmed email and webhook subscriptions with per-component selection, cookieless tokens, one-click unsubscribe, and bounce handling.
Per-update channel selection, bounded retry, exactly-once delivery per subscriber per update, and a filterable delivery log.
Signed webhooks from monitoring tools that create deduplicated draft incidents and never touch a public surface on their own.
An incident brief of what is known and not known, and an optional AI suggestion that fills the composer from it, never published without an operator.
Equal operators with no roles, and attribution recorded on every action that reaches the public record.
Twelve months of public history, one post-incident report per incident, and a complete export.
Website-first setup, Lamp's own live checks, and owner-terminal issuance of native single-use sign-in links.
Owner move-in from a hosted status page: dry run, retroactive import with one subscriber invitation, idempotent re-run and undo through Base's import kit.

nonGoals: Uptime monitoring, probing, or synthetic checks: Lamp reports state that operators or accepted alerts produce, and running probes would make it a monitoring product with a second, contradictory source of truth behind the public page. For observability, see [Porthole](https://github.com/just-every/run-porthole).
On-call scheduling, paging, and escalation: the buyer's existing alerting tool already does this, and it is the system that feeds INTAKE-001.
More than one status page per deployment: one business gets one public record, so a second page is a second deployment.

Private or audience-scoped status pages: visitor authentication would be a whole second access surface for a product whose value is being readable by anyone, at any time, with nothing between them and it.
Roles and permissions: these are one business's equal operators, and UPDATE-007 covers the one gate buyers actually ask for.
SMS and voice notifications: per-message cost, carrier registration, and per-country consent rules that a self-hosted deployment cannot satisfy generically.
Multi-language status pages: every incident update would need a translation before publish, which is the opposite of publishing in two minutes.
A general-purpose operator API authenticated by API tokens: BASE-ACCESS-002 requires a session on every operator endpoint, and machine writes have one narrow door, INTAKE-001, with its own secret.

SCIM and role synchronization: optional OpenID Connect through Auth, Google, Microsoft or Okta replaces the former SSO exclusion under ACCESS-002; provider sign-in stays off until the owner links and enables it, and magic links remain available.

Visitor analytics and email open tracking: BASE-PUBLIC-001 keeps the page free of cookies and visitor data, and NOTIFY-004 keeps tracking pixels out of notifications, because knowing who read an outage notice is worth less than being the one page a customer can open without being counted.
Native mobile apps: the public page is the mobile experience, and it has to work with script disabled.

externals.why: SETUP-002, at the owner's request: read the supplied public website, its declared manifest and mark, and its public status page, the one it links to or one answering at status.<its domain>. An identified Statuspage, Instatus or Better Stack page's own public feeds (Statuspage /api/v2/summary.json and /api/v2/incidents.json; Instatus /summary.json, /v2/components.json and /history.atom; Better Stack /index.json and /feed) give its components, groups, page ID and past incidents; only when the owner chooses Bring its incident history too are they read once more and imported through Move in, as MOVE-002's silent history. Public DNS-over-HTTPS at cloudflare-dns.com validates every destination and redirect; private addresses are refused. No source key is used.
data: Owner-supplied website URL and linked public resource URLs
Destination hostnames for public DNS resolution

externals.why: Cloudflare Workers cannot deliver email to arbitrary recipients. Subscriber notification is the product's second surface, and SUB-006 and NOTIFY-008 require authenticated bulk sending with List-Unsubscribe support. Managed hosting uses the declared Run Edit Run relay with an installation credential; ordinary hosting uses Resend, SendGrid, Mailgun, Amazon SES or Postmark directly. An explicitly configured secondary receives the same frozen envelope after five minutes of retryable primary rejections; an uncertain primary submission never switches providers.
data: Subscriber email address
The published update's fields
The subscription's unsubscribe and management tokens

externals.why: DRAFT-001 only. Absent, the composer shows no suggestion control and no request is made (DRAFT-003). Internal notes are never sent (DRAFT-002).
data: Incident title
Accepted alert payloads
Published updates
Component states

externals.why: SUB-009. The destinations are chosen by the buyer's subscribers, so they cannot be enumerated as named hosts at publish time; this entry is declared as a class of destinations, not one named service, which satisfies BASE-DATA-004 without a supersession because the payload carries no personal data, every request is signed, and every delivery is in the log.
data: The published update's fields
The delivery identifier
The update identifier

externals.why: NOTIFY-011 and NOTIFY-012: Slack incoming webhooks (hooks.slack.com) and Microsoft Teams channel webhooks (*.logic.azure.com, *.environment.api.powerplatform.com, *.webhook.office.com) receive the published update's public fields. The owner adds each channel; its URL is the credential and is stored encrypted.

The incident reference and title
A link to the incident's public page

Redirects and off-scope pagination are refused. The token is never stored; saved responses need no request.

Status page ID and status report IDs

User-selected element structure
Explicitly reviewed text limited to 240 characters

externals.why: ACCESS-002. Optional owner-linked OpenID Connect through Auth, Google, Microsoft or Okta; disabled until explicitly enabled.

OIDC authorization code and app client authentication

externals.why: Owner-selected independent heartbeat service. Disabled until configured. Cron pings only after scheduled work and database/storage/queue self-check pass.

externals.why: MOVE-001 only, at the owner's request: fixed-origin GET requests to https://api.instatus.com read pages, selected-page components, incidents, maintenance lists/details, subscribers and audience groups. Redirects are refused. The Bearer API key is never stored; saved responses need no request.

Selected page ID and maintenance IDs

externals.why: MOVE-001 only, at the owner’s request: authenticated GET reads from https://api.sorryapp.com/v1/pages or keyless GET reads from the selected public Sorry HTTPS page. Redirects are refused; pagination stays on the selected collection. Keys are used only for the read and never stored. Saved responses make no network request.

externals.why: INTAKE-009: when the owner connects a sealed REST API key, each linked publication posts one note to the fixed https://api.pagerduty.com REST host. Redirects are refused. No connected key means no request.

PagerDuty user email in the From header
The published update text and incident permalink
The linked PagerDuty incident ID

externals.why: Slack and Teams incident commands: bounded credential-free GET requests to https://login.botframework.com/v1/.well-known/openidconfiguration and its same-origin signing keys verify Bot Framework activity tokens. Redirects are refused. No user data or token is sent.

externals.why: SUB-014: only a visitor-initiated Slack OAuth v2 exchange POST to https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access; requests only incoming-webhook. Redirects are refused. The returned webhook is encrypted and used only for the approved subscription.

Slack team and selected channel identifiers; public notification fields

externals.why: INTAKE-014: explicit JSM connection reads cloudId without credentials from its validated HTTPS *.atlassian.net/_edge/tenant_info. Published linked updates send notes and optional resolve-close only to fixed https://api.atlassian.com/jsm/ops/api or https://api.opsgenie.com/v2/alerts; redirects are refused.

Connected Atlassian account email in Basic Authorization only
Published update text, incident permalink and linked alert ID

externals.why: UPTIME-008 and INTAKE-011: after an Owner or Admin connects a read-only key, query Datadog, New Relic, Pingdom or an owner-supplied public HTTPS Prometheus-compatible endpoint. Requests read aggregate values only, refuse redirects and private destinations, and never send subscriber or incident data. Query keys are sealed and excluded from archives.
data: Owner-configured metric query, account or check ID and time window
Owner-supplied read-only provider key

externals.why: SUB-013 and NOTIFY-014: an owner-configured Twilio account sends opt-in, keyword replies and approved status publications. SMS stays off without provider configuration; signed callbacks record consent and delivery without tracking.
data: Subscriber phone number
Page name and consent wording
Published update text and permanent link

externals.why: INTEG-002: owner-selected updates post to X at https://api.x.com, Bluesky at https://bsky.social and Mastodon at https://mastodon.social. Owner-chosen Bluesky service hosts and Mastodon instances are a destination class: public HTTPS origins only, private/internal addresses and redirects refused, with Worker global_fetch_strictly_public enforcing resolved-address safety. X uses an owner-supplied OAuth 2.0 user token with tweet.write; Bluesky uses an app password; Mastodon uses a token with write:statuses. Credentials are sealed and never returned or logged.
data: Owner's posting credential sent only to its chosen network authentication endpoint or in Authorization
Owner prefix, published lifecycle and customer-impact statement
Incident or maintenance permalink and prior network post identifiers

env.name: CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID
env.why: pnpm setup uses this owner-controlled account to query and provision deterministic D1, R2, and Queue resources.

env.name: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
env.why: pnpm setup uses this owner-controlled token only for Cloudflare resource provisioning.

env.name: LAMP_PAGE_HOST
env.why: The hostname the public status page is served on at / (PAGE-012); the company points its own name, such as status.company.com, at it.

env.name: LAMP_APP_HOST
env.why: The hostname the Lamp landing page (its /), the operator app and sign-in are served on. It must differ from the page host, so each host has its own home page and PAGE-008 can be applied to one and BASE-ACCESS-003 to the other.

env.name: LAMP_PAGE_NAME
env.why: Initial persisted public page name created by pnpm setup (PAGE-012).

env.name: LAMP_PAGE_TAGLINE
env.why: Initial persisted public page tagline created by pnpm setup (PAGE-012).

env.name: LAMP_PAGE_TIMEZONE
env.why: Initial persisted IANA timezone created by pnpm setup (PAGE-012).

env.name: LAMP_ACCENT_COLOR
env.why: Initial persisted six-digit public accent colour created by pnpm setup (PAGE-012).

env.name: MAIL_PROVIDER_API_KEY
env.why: Required for ordinary Resend, SendGrid, Mailgun, SES or Postmark mail only. mail.sender.v1.

env.name: MAIL_PROVIDER
env.why: Select rer for managed relay mail, resend (default), sendgrid, mailgun, ses or postmark for mail.sender.v1. SES credentials use JSON containing accessKeyId, secretAccessKey and optional sessionToken. Hosted mail must be configured.

env.name: SENDGRID_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY
env.why: Base64 ECDSA public key for signed SendGrid delivery receipts; SendGrid feedback rejects callbacks when omitted.

env.name: MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS
env.why: Required for ordinary Resend, SendGrid, Mailgun, SES or Postmark mail only. NOTIFY-008.

env.name: MAIL_DKIM_SELECTOR
env.why: Required for ordinary Resend, SendGrid, Mailgun, SES or Postmark mail only. NOTIFY-010 DNS preflight identifies the provider-published DKIM selector for MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS.

env.name: RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.why: Optional Resend provider-feedback signature secret. When omitted, provider feedback endpoints reject callbacks as unconfigured.

env.name: SUBSCRIBER_TOKEN_SECRET
env.why: Signs the opaque subscriber tokens in SUB-005.

env.name: WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET
env.why: Signs outbound subscriber webhooks (SUB-009).

env.name: SETUP_OPERATOR_EMAIL
env.why: The operator created at setup (TEAM-002).

env.name: AI_PROVIDER_URL
env.why: ai.provider.v1 OpenAI-compatible HTTPS endpoint. It is configured only with AI_PROVIDER_API_KEY and AI_PROVIDER_MODEL.

env.name: AI_PROVIDER_API_KEY
env.why: ai.provider.v1 credential. It is configured only with AI_PROVIDER_URL and AI_PROVIDER_MODEL.

env.name: AI_PROVIDER_MODEL
env.why: ai.provider.v1 model identifier. It is configured only with AI_PROVIDER_URL and AI_PROVIDER_API_KEY.

env.name: RER_MAIL_RELAY_SECRET
env.why: Optional per-product HMAC secret for an owner-operated signed mail-event relay; direct SendGrid signature verification remains available without a relay.

env.name: SETUP_TOKEN
env.why: Random secret of at least 32 characters for the one-time Base owner claim. Retain for installer setup/deploy commands; the durable claim prevents reuse against an initialized store.

env.name: SESSION_SECRET
env.why: Stable random secret of at least 32 characters for Base operator session and link hashes. Installer generates and preserves it.

env.name: IDENTITY_PROVIDER
env.why: Optional Auth installation URL for the oidc-provider@1 dependency.

env.name: AUTH_PROVIDERS
env.why: Optional Base provider configuration JSON, including private client credentials and explicit subject associations.

env.name: OIDC_TRANSACTION_SECRET
env.why: Independent stable random secret for optional OpenID Connect transactions.

env.name: LAMP_HEARTBEAT_URL
env.why: Public HTTPS heartbeat capability URL chosen by the owner; empty disables pings.

env.name: LAMP_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MINUTES
env.why: Heartbeat interval on the cron minute grid; defaults to five minutes.

env.name: MAIL_FROM
env.why: Required when MAIL_PROVIDER is rer. Run Edit Run assigns the verified managed sender; Lamp uses it as the product sender address.

env.name: MAIL_RELAY_URL
env.why: Required when MAIL_PROVIDER is rer. HTTPS Run Edit Run managed mail endpoint; never follows redirects.

env.name: MAIL_API_KEY
env.why: Required when MAIL_PROVIDER is rer. Private installation and environment credential for the managed mail relay.

env.name: SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET
env.why: Verifies the exact bytes of incoming Slack incident commands. Without it the Slack door is unavailable.

env.name: SLACK_CLIENT_ID
env.why: Optional Slack OAuth v2 client identifier for visitor-initiated incoming-webhook subscriptions.

env.name: SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET
env.why: Optional Slack OAuth v2 client secret; only used for the visitor-approved incoming-webhook exchange.

env.name: BOT_FRAMEWORK_APP_ID
env.why: The required token audience for incoming Teams incident commands. Without it the Teams door is unavailable.

env.name: BOT_FRAMEWORK_APP_PASSWORD
env.why: Reserved bot registration password. Incoming invoke responses use no outbound Bot Framework call and never read this password.

env.name: MAIL_SECONDARY_PROVIDER
env.why: Optional secondary direct provider: resend, sendgrid, mailgun, ses or postmark, different from the primary. Configure with MAIL_SECONDARY_API_KEY. Explicit retryable rejections for five minutes permit failover; ambiguous submissions never switch providers.

env.name: MAIL_SECONDARY_API_KEY
env.why: Optional secondary provider credential; required with MAIL_SECONDARY_PROVIDER.

env.name: MAILGUN_REGION
env.why: Mailgun API region: us (default) or eu. Both primary and secondary Mailgun use this selection.

env.name: MAILGUN_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY
env.why: Dedicated Mailgun HTTP webhook signing key. Signed delivery, bounce and complaint callbacks are refused when omitted.

env.name: SES_REGION
env.why: AWS region for the SES v2 sending identity and SigV4 requests; required for a selected SES provider.

env.name: SES_CONFIGURATION_SET
env.why: SES configuration set whose SNS event destination publishes delivery, bounce and complaint events; required for a selected SES provider.

env.name: SES_EVENT_TOPIC_ARN
env.why: Exact SNS topic trusted for native SES events. Only SHA-256-signed SNS Notifications from its regional HTTPS certificate endpoint are accepted.

env.name: POSTMARK_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.why: Postmark HTTPS Basic-auth password for webhook user lamp. Postmark does not provide a native payload signature; this authentication is not claimed as signed-event proof.

env.name: POSTMARK_ACCOUNT_API_KEY
env.why: Optional Postmark account-level token used only to read sender-domain DKIM verification. Sending uses the separate server token in the selected provider key.

env.name: TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID
env.why: Twilio account identifier for the owner-configured SMS sender; absent keeps SMS off.

env.name: TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
env.why: Twilio authentication token for sending SMS and verifying signed inbound replies and delivery callbacks.

env.name: TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER
env.why: Twilio registered E.164 sending number, used when no messaging service is configured.

env.name: TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE
env.why: Twilio Messaging Service identifier used instead of a sending number when configured.

deploy.notes: Two distinct hostnames share this one deployment, and each has its own home page at /; equal hostnames fail at startup. LAMP_PAGE_HOST serves the public-page paths: /, /history, /incidents/, /maintenance/, /history.atom and imported source shortlink paths, /feed.atom, /widget.js, /api/public/status, and /assets/ are read-only and served from the PAGE-005 snapshot, exempt from BASE-ACCESS-003 rate limiting per PAGE-008; /subscribe, /confirm-subscription/, /unsubscribe/, /manage/, and /api/intake/ are subscription or intake paths rate limited under BASE-ACCESS-003. LAMP_APP_HOST serves the operator app, mounted at /app behind a session, plus its public paths: / (the Lamp landing page, a static document that needs no session), /docs and /docs/ (the product's own docs, drawn from the repository's Markdown at build time and public like the landing page; the page host has none), /health, /signin, /auth/, /.well-known/rer-*, /app-assets/, and /_serverFn/. With Run Edit Run's owner-claim trust configured it also serves Business's signed routes, POST only and 404 without that trust: /api/rer/import/ (the Business import door, off until the owner allows it) and /api/rer/cutover-status, a read-only RER grant of action cutover-status under the owner-claim key ring that answers a move's old-address, count, subscriber, created-since and intake-receipt figures (counts and ids only). /lamp, the landing page's former address, answers 301 to / on the app host for one release and is then removed. /_serverFn/ is TanStack Start's opaque generated transport, restricted to the app host and protected by Start's same-origin checks; every private handler independently validates the native operator session before returning data. The one exception is the docs page-body handler, which returns the same public text as /docs. It is not a PAGE-008 public read or rate-limit exemption. Two of the page host's write paths key their rate limit on the subscriber token rather than the caller's address: /unsubscribe, because one-click unsubscribe arrives from a mailbox provider's shared egress and a per-address limit would break it for every subscriber behind that address (SUB-006), and /manage/ for the same reason, since it is reached from the same emailed link. The public page host also accepts SMS subscription POST /subscribe/sms and the exact Twilio callback POST paths /api/public/sms/inbound and /api/public/sms/status. Each callback requires a valid X-Twilio-Signature over its complete public URL and body fields; SMS Settings and delivery records remain on authenticated /api/app/sms/ paths on the operator host.

limits.status: Mixed evidence: limits marked estimate:true are modeled or locally measured only and still require deployment- or account-specific validation; estimate:false values are enforced configuration limits. Each entry records its evidence.

subscribers.why: A local authenticated publish and native scheduled trigger persisted 1,000 unique fake-provider acceptances. The fake network used a strict 10-acceptance/second quota and 100ms acknowledgement; peak acceptance was 9/second, p95 completion was 185.474 seconds, and the last acceptance arrived in 191.362 seconds, including 64.488 seconds waiting for the trigger. This remains an estimate: it does not qualify a live provider account, quota, latency, domain configuration, or recipient delivery.

components.why: Qualified in a populated local Worker fixture with 200 components and 25 groups. This is a representative record count; arbitrary component text and worst-case snapshot bytes remain unqualified.

componentGroups.why: Qualified alongside 200 components in a populated local Worker fixture. This is a representative group count, not a bound on arbitrary data size.

openIncidents.why: Qualified with 25 open incidents; all 25 titles appeared on the public page. This is representative content, not a worst-case history-size limit.

incidentUpdatesPerIncident.why: Qualified with 200 updates on an incident; the full public timeline showed all 200 update markers. This is representative history, not a bound on arbitrary update bytes.

publicPageRequestsPerSecond.why: Local floor, not a hosted capacity. One Miniflare workerd process on a shared runner was driven in-process at an offered 10 requests/second with uncompressed responses and no CDN: two fresh 30-second full-page runs and two mixed-route runs each returned 300/300 HTTP 200 with no backlog (full-page p95 880.289ms and 312.709ms; mixed-route p95 138.466ms and 112.200ms). Full-page runs at 20/s fell behind on that runner; mixed routes held 20/s. A 5,000/s local attempt failed with loopback connection resets in the load client and does not bound the Worker. On Cloudflare every public read runs the Worker, which reads the R2 current pointer and serves edge-cached generation bytes; that hosted capacity is unmeasured, and no runtime rate limiter was added.

subscribeRequestsPerMinutePerAddress.why: Rate limit on a BASE-ACCESS-003 write path; not a capacity number.

intakeRequestsPerMinutePerSource.why: A paced local run accepted 120 signed intake requests, each with HTTP 202, and durably recorded their draft incidents while the public status remained unchanged. This qualifies that fixture and path only; deployment throughput remains unvalidated.

uploadMaxBytes.why: Page logos and header images; WOFF2 theme fonts have a stricter 512KB limit (BASE-INPUT-003).

uploadTypes.why: No SVG: BASE-INPUT-002 would have to sanitise a scripting format for one logo, on the one surface that must never run anything unexpected.

subscriptionCapacity.why: SUB-020: atomic storage guards count pending and active subscriptions across all channels; deactivated and deleted subscriptions do not count. This is an admission limit; the separate subscribers entry qualifies notification delivery only.

webhookSubscriptions.why: SUB-020: webhook endpoint admission limit within the all-channel capacity.

chatSubscriptions.why: SUB-020: Slack and Teams subscriptions share this admission limit within the all-channel capacity.

accessibility.status: Automated Axe WCAG 2.2 AA checks run in pnpm verify against test-owned local public status, permanent incident/history and valid subscription-token pages, sign-in, every current authenticated operator route, and an allow-listed widget surface. They do not replace manual keyboard or assistive-technology review, which remains outstanding.

operatingCost.status: computed from published Cloudflare Workers Free/Paid pricing tiers and the stated usage assumptions, not measured against a running deployment
operatingCost.basis: The low-volume default is USD 0/month on Workers Free: 100,000 Worker requests/day, 10,000 Queues operations/day, D1's 5 million reads/day and 100,000 writes/day, the R2 free tier, Cron, and SQLite-backed Durable Objects including alarms. A local public-read measurement does not establish Workers Free or Paid deployment capacity; USD 5/month is the Paid minimum, not a sustained-load estimate. Transactional mail and optional AI remain excluded.
